properties.name: Casas Grandes (Paquimé)
properties.subtitle: Chihuahua, Mexico
properties.claim: A multi-storey adobe city with piped water, subterranean reservoirs, macaw breeding pens and T-shaped doorways matching Chaco Canyon's, built in the middle of a desert and abandoned, is presented as a planted settlement linking two regions.
properties.context: Paquimé is a World Heritage site excavated by Charles Di Peso, and its Chaco and Mesoamerican connections are the mainstream interpretation: it was a trading centre between the Puebloan south-west and West Mexico, moving copper bells, shell and scarlet macaws north. The macaw pens and the water system are real engineering by the Casas Grandes culture, with regional antecedents.
properties.summary: Casas Grandes (Spanish for Great Houses; also known as Paquimé) is a prehistoric archaeological site in the northern Mexican state of Chihuahua. Construction of the site is attributed to the Mogollon culture. Casas Grandes has been designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site under the purview of INAH and a "Pueblo Mágico" since 2015.
